vsm1.3:27.1: (vii) How should it be developed? A. DEVELOPMENT IN BRIEF
vsm1.3:27.2:
The method of developing the kind of concentration associated with the noble paths mentioned
(§7) under that “of two kinds as mundane and supramundane,” etc.,
vsm1.3:27.3: is included in the method of developing understanding;
vsm1.3:27.4: (Ch. XXII) for in developing path understanding that is developed too.
vsm1.3:27.5: So we shall say nothing separately here about how that is to be developed.
vsm1.3:28.1: But mundane concentration should be developed
vsm1.3:28.2: by one who has taken his stand on virtue that is quite purified in the way already stated.
vsm1.3:28.3: He should sever any of the ten impediments that he may have.
vsm1.3:28.4: He should then approach the good friend, the giver of a meditation subject,
vsm1.3:28.5: and he should apprehend from among the forty meditation subjects one that suits his own temperament.
vsm1.3:28.6: After that he should avoid a monastery unfavourable to the development of concentration and go to live in one that is favourable.
vsm1.3:28.7: Then he should sever the lesser impediments and not overlook any of the directions for development. This is in brief.
vsm1.3:29.1: B. DEVELOPMENT IN DETAIL The detail is this:
vsm1.3:29.2: Firstly it was said above, he should sever any of the ten impediments that he may have. Now, the “ten impediments” are:
vsm1.3:29.3:
A dwelling, family, and gain,
A class, and building too as fifth,
vsm1.3:29.4:
And travel, kin, affliction, books,
And supernormal powers: ten.
vsm1.3:29.5: Herein, the dwelling itself is the “impediment due to the dwelling.” So too with the family and so on.
vsm1.3:30.1: 1. Herein, a single inner room or a single hut or a whole monastery for the Community is called a dwelling.
vsm1.3:30.2: This is not an impediment for everyone.
vsm1.3:30.3: It is an impediment only for anyone whose mind is exercised about the building, etc., that goes on there,
vsm1.3:30.4: or who has many belongings stored there,
vsm1.3:30.5: or whose mind is caught up by some business connected with it.
vsm1.3:30.6: For any other it is not an impediment.
vsm1.3:31.1: Here is a relevant story. Two clansmen left Anurādhapura, it seems, and eventually went forth at the Thūpārāma.
vsm1.3:31.2: One of them made himself familiar with the Two Codes,
vsm1.3:31.3: and when he had acquired five years’ seniority, he took part in the Pavāraṇā
vsm1.3:31.4: and then left for the place called Pācīnakhaṇḍarājī.
vsm1.3:31.5: The other stayed on where he was.
vsm1.3:31.6: Now, when the one who had gone to Pācīnakhaṇḍarājī had lived there a long time and had become an elder, he thought,
vsm1.3:31.7: “This place is good for retreat; suppose I told my friend about it?”
vsm1.3:31.8: So he set out, and in due course he entered the Thūpārāma.
vsm1.3:31.9: As he entered, the elder of the same seniority saw him, went to meet him, took his bowl and robe and did the duties.
vsm1.3:32.1: The visiting elder went into his lodging. He thought,
vsm1.3:32.2: “Now my friend will be sending me ghee or molasses or a drink;
vsm1.3:32.3: for he has lived long in this city.”
vsm1.3:32.4: He got nothing that night, and in the morning he thought,
vsm1.3:32.5: “Now he will be sending me rice gruel and solid food sent by his supporters.”
vsm1.3:32.6: When he saw none, he thought, “There is no one to bring it. No doubt they will give it when we go into the town.”
vsm1.3:32.7: Early in the morning they went into the town together.
vsm1.3:32.8: When they had wandered through one street and had got only a ladleful of gruel, they sat down in a sitting hall to drink it.
vsm1.3:33.2: “Perhaps there is no individual giving of gruel.
vsm1.3:33.3: But as soon as it is the time for the meal people will give special food.”
vsm1.3:33.4: But when it was time for the meal, they ate what they had got by wandering for alms.
vsm1.3:33.5: Then the visitor said, “Venerable sir, how is this? Do you live in this way all the time?”
vsm1.3:33.6: —“Yes, friend.”—”Venerable sir, Pācīnakhaṇḍarājī is comfortable; let us go there.”
vsm1.3:33.7: Now, as the elder came out from the city by the southern gate
vsm1.3:33.8: he took the Kumbhakāragāma road which leads to Pācīnakhaṇḍarājī.
vsm1.3:33.9: The visitor asked, “But, venerable sir, why do you take this road?”—”Did you not recommend Pācīnakhaṇḍarājī, friend?”
vsm1.3:33.10: —”But how is this, venerable sir, have you no extra belongings in the place you have lived in for so long?”
vsm1.3:33.11: —”That is so, friend. The bed and chair belong to the Community, and they are put away as usual. There is nothing else.”
vsm1.3:33.12: —”But, venerable sir, I have left my staff and my oil tube and my sandal bag there.”
vsm1.3:33.13: —”Have you already collected so much, friend, living there for just one day?”—“Yes, venerable sir.”
vsm1.3:34.1: He was glad in his heart, and he paid homage to the elder: “For those like you, venerable sir, everywhere is a forest dwelling.
vsm1.3:34.2: The Thūpārāma is a place where the relics of four Buddhas are deposited;
vsm1.3:34.3: there is suitable hearing of the Dhamma in the Brazen Palace;
vsm1.3:34.4: there is the Great Shrine to be seen;
vsm1.3:34.6: It is like the time of the Buddha.
vsm1.3:34.7: It is here that you should live.” On the following day he took his bowl and outer robe and went away by himself.
vsm1.3:34.8: It is no impediment for one like that.
vsm1.3:35.1: 2. Family means a family consisting of relatives or of supporters.
vsm1.3:35.2: For even a family consisting of supporters is an impediment
vsm1.3:35.3: for someone who lives in close association with it in the way beginning, “He is pleased when they are pleased” (S III 11),
vsm1.3:35.4: and who does not even go to a neighbouring monastery to hear the Dhamma without members of the family.
vsm1.3:36.1: But even mother and father are not an impediment for another,
vsm1.3:36.2: as in the case of the young bhikkhu, the nephew of the elder who lived at the Koraṇḍaka Monastery.
vsm1.3:36.3: He went to Rohaṇa for instruction, it seems.
vsm1.3:36.4: The elder’s sister, who was a lay devotee, was always asking the elder how her son was getting on.
vsm1.3:36.5: One day the elder set out for Rohaṇa to fetch him back.
vsm1.3:37.1: The young bhikkhu too thought, “I have lived here for a long time.
vsm1.3:37.2: Now I might go and visit my preceptor and find out how the lay devotee is,”
vsm1.3:37.4: The two met on the banks of the Mahaveli River.
vsm1.3:37.5: He did the duties to the elder at the foot of a tree. When asked, “Where are you going?” he told him his purpose.
vsm1.3:37.6: The elder said: “You have done well.
vsm1.3:37.7: The lay devotee is always asking after you.
vsm1.3:37.9: You may go, but I shall stay here for the Rains,” and he dismissed him.
vsm1.3:37.10: He arrived at the monastery on the actual day for taking up residence for the Rains.
vsm1.3:37.11: The lodging allotted to him happened to be the one for which his father had undertaken responsibility.
vsm1.3:38.1: His father came on the following day and asked, “To whom was our lodging allotted, venerable sirs?”
vsm1.3:38.2: When he heard that it had fallen to a young visitor,
vsm1.3:38.3: he went to him. After paying homage to him, he said,
vsm1.3:38.4: “Venerable sir, there is an obligation for him who has taken up residence for the Rains in our lodging.”
vsm1.3:38.6:
—”It is to take alms food only in our house for the three months, and to let us
know the time of departure after the Pavāraṇā ceremony.”
vsm1.3:38.8: The lay devotee went home and told his wife.
vsm1.3:38.9:
“There is a visiting lord who has taken up residence for the Rains in our lodging.
He must be carefully looked after,” and she agreed.
vsm1.3:38.10: She prepared good food of various kinds for him.
vsm1.3:38.11: Though the youth went to his relatives’ home at the time of the meal, no one recognized him.
vsm1.3:39.1: When he had eaten alms food there during the three months
vsm1.3:39.2: and had completed the residence for the Rains,
vsm1.3:39.4: Then his relatives said, “Let it be tomorrow, venerable sir,”
vsm1.3:39.5:
and on the following day, when they had fed him in their house and filled his oil
tube and given him a lump of sugar and a nine-cubit length of cloth,
vsm1.3:39.6: they said, “Now you are leaving, venerable sir.”
vsm1.3:39.7: He gave his blessing and set out for Rohaṇa.
vsm1.3:40.1: His preceptor had completed the Pavāraṇā ceremony and was on his way back. They met at the same place as before.
vsm1.3:40.2: He did the duties to the elder at the foot of a tree.
vsm1.3:40.3: The elder asked him, “How was it, my dear, did you see the good woman lay devotee?”
vsm1.3:40.4: He replied, “Yes, venerable sir,” and he told him all that had happened.
vsm1.3:40.5: He then anointed the elder’s feet with the oil, made him a drink with the sugar, and presented him with the length of cloth.
vsm1.3:40.6: He then, after paying homage to the elder, told him, “Venerable sir, only Rohaṇa suits me,” and he departed.
vsm1.3:40.7: The elder too arrived back at his monastery, and next day he went into the village of Koraṇḍaka.
vsm1.3:41.1: The lay devotee, his sister, had always kept looking down the road, thinking, “My brother is now coming with my son.”
vsm1.3:41.2: When she saw him coming alone, she thought,
vsm1.3:41.3: “My son must be dead; that is why the elder is coming alone,”
vsm1.3:41.4: and she fell at the elder’s feet, lamenting and weeping.
vsm1.3:41.5: Suspecting that it must have been out of fewness of wishes that the youth had gone away without announcing himself,
vsm1.3:41.6: the elder comforted her and told her all that had happened,
vsm1.3:41.7: and he took the length of cloth out of his bag and showed it to her.
vsm1.3:42.2: She prostrated herself in the direction taken by her son, and she said:
vsm1.3:42.3: “Surely the Blessed One taught the way of the Rathavinīta,
vsm1.3:42.6:
and the way of the great Noble Ones’ heritages showing contentment with the four
requisites and delight in development, making a bhikkhu such as my son a body-witness.
vsm1.3:42.7: So, although for three months he ate in the house of the mother who bore him,
vsm1.3:42.8: yet he never said ‘I am your son, you are my mother!’
vsm1.3:42.10: Even mother and father are no impediment for one such as him, so how much less any other family that supports him.
vsm1.3:43.3: Wherever a meritorious bhikkhu goes, people give him a large supply of requisites.
vsm1.3:43.4: With giving blessings to them and teaching them the Dhamma he gets no chance to do the ascetic’s duties.
vsm1.3:43.5: From sunrise till the first watch of the night he never breaks his association with people.
vsm1.3:43.6: Again, even at dawn, alms-food eaters fond of opulence come and say,
vsm1.3:43.7: “Venerable sir, such and such a man lay follower, woman lay follower, friend, friend’s daughter, wants to see you,”
vsm1.3:43.8: and being ready to go, he replies, “Take the bowl and robe, friend.”
vsm1.3:43.9: So he is always on the alert.
vsm1.3:43.10: Thus these requisites are an impediment for him.
vsm1.3:43.11: He should leave his group and wander by himself where he is not known.
vsm1.3:43.12: This is the way his impediment is severed.
vsm1.3:44.1: 4. Class is a class (group) of students of suttas or students of Abhidhamma.
vsm1.3:44.2: If with the group’s instruction and questioning he gets no opportunity for the ascetic’s duties,
vsm1.3:44.3: then that group is an impediment for him.
vsm1.3:44.4: He should sever that impediment in this way:
vsm1.3:44.5: if those bhikkhus have already acquired the main part and little still remains,
vsm1.3:44.6: he should finish that off and then go to the forest.
vsm1.3:44.7: If they have only acquired little and much still remains,
vsm1.3:44.8: he should, without travelling more than a league, approach another instructor of a class within the radius of a league
vsm1.3:44.9: and say, “Help those venerable ones with instruction, etc.”
vsm1.3:44.10: If he does not find anyone in this way,
vsm1.3:44.11: he should take leave of the class, saying. “I have a task to see to, friends; go where it suits you,”
vsm1.3:44.12: and he should do his own work.
vsm1.3:45.2: Since one engaged in this must know about what material has and has not been got by carpenters, etc.,
vsm1.3:45.3: and must see about what has and has not been done,
vsm1.3:45.5: It should be severed in this way. If little remains it should be completed.
vsm1.3:45.7:
it should be handed over to the Community or to bhikkhus who are entrusted with the Community’s
affairs, if it is a new building for the Community;
vsm1.3:45.8: or if it is for himself, it should be handed over to those whom he entrusts with his own affairs,
vsm1.3:45.9: but if these are not available, he should relinquish it to the Community and depart.
vsm1.3:46.1: 6. Travel is going on a journey.
vsm1.3:46.2: If someone is expected to give the going forth somewhere else,
vsm1.3:46.3: or if some requisite is obtainable there and he cannot rest content without getting it
vsm1.3:46.4: that will be an impediment; for even if he goes into the forest to do the ascetic’s duties,
vsm1.3:46.5: he will find it hard to get rid of thoughts about the journey.
vsm1.3:46.6: So one in this position should apply himself to the ascetic’s duties after he has done the journey and transacted the business.
vsm1.3:47.1:
7. Kin in the case of the monastery means teacher, preceptor, co-resident, pupil,
those with the same preceptor as oneself, and those with the same teacher as oneself;
vsm1.3:47.2: and in the case of the house it means mother, father, brother, and so on.
vsm1.3:47.3: When they are sick they are an impediment for him. Therefore that impediment should be severed by curing them with nursing.
vsm1.3:48.1: Herein, when the preceptor is sick he must be cared for as long as life lasts if the sickness does not soon depart.
vsm1.3:48.2: Likewise the teacher at the going forth, the teacher at the admission, the co-resident,
vsm1.3:48.3: the pupils to whom one has given the admission and the going forth, and those who have the same preceptor.
vsm1.3:48.4:
But the teacher from whom one takes the dependence, the teacher who gives one instruction, the pupil to whom one has given
the dependence, the pupil to whom one is giving instruction, and those who have that same teacher as oneself,
vsm1.3:48.5: should be looked after as long as the dependence or the instruction has not been terminated.
vsm1.3:48.6: If one is able to do so, one should look after them even beyond that period.
vsm1.3:49.1: Mother and father should be treated like the preceptor;
vsm1.3:49.2: if they live within the kingdom and look to their son for help, it should be given.
vsm1.3:49.3: Also if they have no medicine, he should give them his own.
vsm1.3:49.4: If he has none, he should go in search of it as alms and give that.
vsm1.3:49.5: But in the case of brothers or sisters, one should only give them what is theirs.
vsm1.3:49.6: If they have none, then one should give one’s own temporarily and later get it back,
vsm1.3:49.7: but one should not complain if one does not get it back.
vsm1.3:49.8: It is not allowed either to make medicine for or to give it to a sister’s husband who is not related by blood;
vsm1.3:49.9: but one can give it to one’s sister saying, “Give it to your husband.”
vsm1.3:49.10: The same applies to one’s brother’s wife.
vsm1.3:49.11: But it is allowed to make it for their children since they are blood relatives.
vsm1.3:50.1: 8. Affliction is any kind of illness.
vsm1.3:50.2: It is an impediment when it is actually afflicting; therefore it should be severed by treatment with medicine.
vsm1.3:50.3: But if it is not cured after taking medicine for a few days,
vsm1.3:50.4: then the ascetic’s duties should be done after apostrophizing one’s person in this way: “I am not your slave, or your hireling.
vsm1.3:50.5: I have come to suffering through maintaining you through the beginningless round of rebirths.”
